pageProps.title: The Therapist
pageProps.review: A review of B. A. Paris's novel The Therapist, an essay analyzing the charm of a psychological thriller by dealing with meticulous foreshadowing and twists surrounding a past incident, the protagonist's suspicion, and the difficulties of a psychological counselor.
pageProps.content:
## Review The foreshadowing was well laid out for the twist. The protagonist distrusts and suspects everyone regarding a past incident.
Indeed, a person who knows a lot attracts a lot of suspicion and jealousy. Being a ```psychological counselor``` is clearly not an easy job.
The setting where the protagonist solves a case that the police missed in the past by herself is forced, but it seems unavoidable in this kind of novel. Let's just say the protagonist is smart.
